what: LyondellBasell makes plastics and chemicals: polyethylene and polypropylene for packaging and products, plus refining and the licensing of its own polymer production technology.
customers: Packaging and consumer goods makers, carmakers, construction materials companies and plastics converters.
money: ethylene, propylene and the plastics made from them
licensing polymer process technology to other producers
moat: World-scale plants using cheap US natural gas liquids, plus a technology licensing business that earns royalties from competitors' plants.
risks: It reported a loss as chemical margins fell to cycle lows
Revenue has fallen about 16% a year over three years
Debt of about $13 billion against $5 billion of cash
European assets have been loss-making and are being closed or sold
opportunities: Analysts see about 25% upside from current levels
Low-cost US feedstock means it is among the last producers to lose money in a downturn
watch: Polyethylene and propylene oxide spreads, and European asset decisions.
